difficulties: None blocking; no entry change needed. (1) make env was not run to completion: it creates a conda env from conda-forge with a fresh package cache in .conda-pkgs, so it needs network downloads; an offline attempt (CONDA_OFFLINE=true make env) failed with PackagesNotFoundError: python=3.12.11. The generator uses only the Python standard library and the Makefile falls back to python3 (3.13.1 here) when .conda/bin/python is absent, so make bench worked unchanged (tests/test_specialized.py, which calls .conda/bin/python directly, was not needed). (2) The Makefile hard-codes mechanisms/ts1.json (no variable), so the file was swapped and then restored; it matches HEAD and git status --porcelain is empty. (3) generator_s is the median of 5 runs including Python startup (about 0.015 s); generated_c_lines is wc -l (the generator writes no final newline). build_s is the wall time of make bench: generation plus three sequential clang compiles (generic bench, specialized bench, specialized scenario runner); TS1 takes 13.2 to 13.5 s. (4) Side check beyond the three mechanisms: a mechanism with no user-defined rates generates empty arrays (4 -Wpedantic warnings: C23 empty initializer, zero-length array), and src/main.c's size check divides by the zero custom-parameter count (undefined behavior); the clang -O3 build still ran and matched the exact solution. (5) Addendum, 64 distinct cells: no difficulty. The same build route and settings were used; TS1 was restored and rebuilt afterwards, and git status --porcelain is clean again.
generated_kernels_evidence: Same code path for 4 and 64 cells, with no cell-count or group-size condition anywhere. src/main.c (shared by both programs) solves the warm-up (line 584) and every timed step (line 605) with chem_rosenbrock3_solve_group_with_workspace on one group of all cells (--threads 1: group_capacity = cells). That function (src/solver.c 804-983) works cell by cell and calls solver_forcing (877, 900), solver_negative_jacobian (880), solver_factor (891) and solver_triangular_solve (914). Each wrapper (src/solver.c 49-66, 365-381) calls m->specialized_ops->... whenever the pointer is non-NULL and otherwise the generic routine; that pointer is the only switch. generated/ts1.c sets chem_generated_mechanism.specialized_ops = &generated_ops under #ifdef CHEM_SPECIALIZED (NULL otherwise), and the Makefile passes -DCHEM_SPECIALIZED only to ts1_bench_specialized and ts1_scenario_specialized. Binary check of each mechanism's build ($WORK/check_ops.py: nm plus dyld_info -fixups, no execution): in ts1_bench_specialized, _chem_generated_mechanism+0x48 rebases to _generated_ops, whose four slots rebase to _generated_forcing, _generated_negative_jacobian, _generated_factor and _generated_solve_factored; ts1_bench_cpu has no _generated_* symbols and no fixup there (NULL). Timing agrees: specialized 4.4x (4 cells) and 4.8x (64 cells) faster on carbon_bond_5, with identical solver counters. Rate constants use the shared generic evaluator in both programs, by design (DESIGN.md). The benchmark has no 32-cell grouping: with --threads 1 the 64 cells form one group with one step controller, as MICM's default run does; only the scenario runner takes --group-size.
